description: Illustrative dispatch policy and triage record for coordinators. Adapt the wording; no triage engine is included. All values are fictional.
announce: Before acting on any request, the first line of the reply is: Decision: <N> <method> | <target> | <one-line reason>. The owner may override it.

1.label: Direct answer
1.when: A read-only question or lookup that takes a few minutes and writes no project file

2.label: Existing session
2.when: The work belongs to a project that has a healthy, idle session for this kind of work
2.who: That session, sent by the domain supervisor

3.label: New session in the project
3.when: There is a project but no suitable session, the session is busy, or parallel work is needed
3.who: A new session in the same project; never two writers on one session

4.label: New worktree
4.when: Git code changes that must be isolated from other work in progress
4.who: An agent in a new worktree

5.label: New project
5.when: A new subject that no existing project fits
5.who: A new project, registered in routing

self_execute_only: System work in a domain the coordinator itself supervises
Work the owner explicitly said 'do it yourself' about
dispatch_message_must_include: The owner's original request and success criteria
Read-only and writable scope, and forbidden actions (submitting, paying, emailing, public sharing, creating accounts)
Whether new terminals or agents may be opened, maximum concurrency and a quota ceiling
The subject of every limit: writer, coordinator, or everyone (e.g. 'new terminals/agents = 0, including the coordinator and its subagents')
Report your own station when done

follow_up.channel: Type follow-ups straight into the writer's terminal through a wrapper that records the relay; mailbox messages are for coordinator-to-coordinator mail and formal worker reports only
follow_up.before_sending: Target idle and input line empty. Grey suggestion (screen shows only the prompt symbol, draft field has text) may be replaced; a real draft (text after the prompt symbol) is never sent over or cleared; ask the owner

record_example.text: Fix the footer link on Website A

inspection: The daily inspection counts recorded decisions by option and names action requests that a coordinator handled itself.
review_dispatch: Read-only: never modify what is being reviewed
Structured findings: location, severity (high/medium/low), evidence, suggestion
If nothing is found, say so; do not pad
The coordinator spot-checks findings before passing them to the owner; quality is not judged by count
